modules.title: Engineering Foundations
modules.subtitle: Think in systems, determinism, failure costs, and human oversight before touching frameworks.
modules.outcome: Map real business processes into inputs, deterministic rules, probabilistic AI boundaries, measurable ROI, and safe human checkpoints.
modules.prerequisiteRationale: Entry foundation for all learners, including experienced n8n builders who want stronger engineering framing.

miniProject.title: Support Triage Process Blueprint
miniProject.brief: Map a noisy support inbox into an engineered workflow: define inputs, outputs, deterministic filters, AI classification boundary, failure cost, and human approval gate.
steps: List every input field arriving on a support email (sender, subject, body, timestamp, customer tier).
Separate deterministic rules (VIP domain check, spam blocklist, duplicate ticket ID) from probabilistic steps (topic classification, draft reply).
Document side effects (sending email, updating CRM, issuing refund) and decide which require human approval.
Calculate baseline time spent per ticket and estimate maximum acceptable error cost for each side effect.
acceptanceCriteria: Process diagram clearly separates deterministic nodes from LLM steps.
Every external side effect has a documented owner and failure-cost rating.
At least two automation candidates are explicitly rejected with written rationale.

masteryChecklist: I can explain the difference between a deterministic workflow and a probabilistic agent.
I can map inputs, outputs, and irreversible side effects before writing code or building nodes.
I can justify when NOT to use AI in an automation pipeline.
I can define human-in-the-loop checkpoints based on failure cost.

modules.title: Computer, Terminal, and Git Foundations
modules.subtitle: Navigate directories, shell processes, environment variables, Git branches, and secret hygiene.
modules.outcome: Operate confidently in a Linux/macOS/WSL terminal, manage Git branches safely without leaking secrets, and read real stack traces.
modules.prerequisiteRationale: Uses the engineering mindset from Module 1 to build safe local development habits before networking and Python.

miniProject.title: Clean Automation Repo Starter
miniProject.brief: Initialize a version-controlled Python automation repository with .gitignore, .env.example, branch workflow, and clean commit history.
steps: Create a project directory using terminal commands and inspect paths with pwd and ls.
Initialize a Git repository, add a strict .gitignore excluding .env and .venv, and create .env.example.
Create a feature branch, add a sample config loader reading an environment variable, and merge via commit.
acceptanceCriteria: git status shows zero tracked secrets or virtual environment directories.
Environment variable configuration is documented in .env.example.
Commit history uses clear, descriptive messages on a non-main branch.

masteryChecklist: I can navigate paths, inspect files, and manage processes from the terminal.
I can configure environment variables without hardcoding credentials.
I can create branches, inspect diffs, and commit safely with Git.
I know how to keep API keys out of Git history and what to do if one leaks.

modules.title: Networking, HTTP, and Hosting
modules.subtitle: Master localhost, ports, DNS, HTTP, TLS, webhooks, proxies, CORS, and Docker container networking.
modules.outcome: Diagnose connection refusals, localhost mismatches, DNS errors, webhook failures, CORS issues, and Docker container bridges systematically.
modules.prerequisiteRationale: Builds on terminal fluency so you can run curl, inspect ports, and troubleshoot container networking.

miniProject.title: HTTP & Docker Connectivity Lab
miniProject.brief: Diagnose and document why an n8n container cannot reach a Python service on localhost, fix the host binding and network route, and verify with curl.
steps: Run a local HTTP listener bound first to 127.0.0.1:8000 and test with curl.
Simulate container-to-host isolation and compare localhost vs host.docker.internal vs Docker bridge service names.
Trace full HTTP request headers, status codes, timeouts, and reverse proxy forwarding headers.
acceptanceCriteria: You can explain why 127.0.0.1 inside container A is not container B or the host machine.
curl test captures method, headers, JSON body, and HTTP status code.
Written troubleshooting checklist covers DNS, connection refused, timeout, and TLS errors.

masteryChecklist: I understand IP addresses, ports, loopback (127.0.0.1), and host binding (0.0.0.0).
I can read HTTP methods, headers, bodies, and status codes (2xx/3xx/4xx/5xx).
I know the difference between authentication and authorization, and what CORS does NOT protect.
I can connect services across Docker networks and behind reverse proxies.

modules.title: Python for Automation
modules.subtitle: Write clean, typed, tested Python code with virtual environments, JSON handling, logging, httpx, and async.
modules.outcome: Build maintainable Python automation scripts and libraries with isolated venvs, explicit exceptions, structured logs, HTTP clients, and unit tests.
modules.prerequisiteRationale: Uses terminal/venv habits from Module 2 and HTTP fundamentals from Module 3 for API client code.

miniProject.title: Typed Support Ticket Cleaner CLI
miniProject.brief: Write a small Python package in a virtual environment that reads raw support ticket JSON files, normalizes fields, enriches via an HTTP API with httpx, logs failures, and passes unit tests.
steps: Create and activate a Python venv and install httpx and pytest.
Implement typed functions to parse JSON payloads, handle malformed inputs cleanly, and log structured events.
Write unit tests covering valid tickets, missing fields, and simulated HTTP timeouts.
acceptanceCriteria: All functions include explicit Python type hints.
Malformed JSON never crashes silently; exceptions are logged with context.
Unit test suite passes cleanly offline using mocked HTTP responses.

masteryChecklist: I isolate every Python project inside its own virtual environment.
I write typed Python functions using dictionaries, lists, exceptions, and pathlib/json.
I use logging instead of scattered print statements.
I can make async/sync HTTP requests with timeouts and write unit tests.

modules.title: APIs and FastAPI
modules.subtitle: Design reliable REST contracts, call external APIs with retries/idempotency, and connect n8n to FastAPI.
modules.outcome: Expose production-style FastAPI endpoints with explicit contracts, bearer auth, retries, idempotency keys, and verified n8n connectivity.
modules.prerequisiteRationale: Combines HTTP mechanics (Module 3) with Python functions, exceptions, and async HTTP clients (Module 4).

miniProject.title: FastAPI Triage Endpoint for n8n
miniProject.brief: Build a FastAPI service with /health and /v1/triage endpoints, bearer token validation, idempotency check, and call it from an n8n HTTP Request node.
steps: Define FastAPI request/response models and implement bearer token header verification.
Add idempotency-key deduplication so retried n8n requests do not create duplicate tickets.
Connect an n8n HTTP Request node (handling localhost vs container network) and debug status codes.
acceptanceCriteria: Requests without valid Authorization bearer token fail with 401.
Duplicate idempotency keys return the cached decision rather than re-running side effects.
n8n HTTP Request node receives deterministic JSON matching the API contract.

masteryChecklist: I design clear API contracts before writing route handlers.
I handle pagination, 429 rate limits, and exponential backoff safely.
I use idempotency keys to protect side effects on retries.
I can connect and debug n8n HTTP Request calls to a FastAPI service.

modules.title: LLM Fundamentals
modules.subtitle: Understand tokens, context limits, sampling, hallucinations, prompt boundaries, structured outputs, and tool calling.
modules.outcome: Call LLM APIs directly without framework magic, enforce strict instruction/data separation, demand structured JSON, and know when NOT to use an LLM.
modules.prerequisiteRationale: Requires engineering cost awareness (M01) and Python HTTP API skills (M04-M05) to call model endpoints directly.

miniProject.title: Direct-API Support Email Classifier
miniProject.brief: Write a plain Python script (no LangChain yet) calling an LLM HTTP API or mock harness to classify support emails into JSON with latency/token tracking.
steps: Separate system instructions from untrusted email body delimiters.
Request structured JSON output and measure token counts and latency per ticket.
Compare deterministic regex/rule pre-filters against LLM classification on 15 test emails.
acceptanceCriteria: No framework wrappers are used; raw HTTP payload and response parsing are explicit.
Untrusted email text is wrapped clearly and never concatenated into system instructions.
Every run records input tokens, output tokens, and latency.

masteryChecklist: I understand tokens, context windows, temperature, and why models hallucinate.
I separate trusted system instructions from untrusted user/external data.
I can explain structured outputs and tool calling as JSON contracts, not magic.
I benchmark direct API calls and avoid putting an LLM in deterministic steps.

modules.title: Pydantic and Data Contracts
modules.subtitle: Enforce runtime validation, nested schemas, enums, validators, JSON Schema, and safe handling of LLM outputs.
modules.outcome: Build airtight data contracts with Pydantic v2 that reject malformed LLM outputs safely and distinguish syntax validity from factual accuracy.
modules.prerequisiteRationale: Connects Python type hints (M04), FastAPI payloads (M05), and structured LLM output needs (M06).

miniProject.title: Support Ticket Contract Validator
miniProject.brief: Create Pydantic v2 models for incoming n8n support webhooks and outgoing LLM triage decisions with Enums, field constraints, cross-field validators, and fallback routing.
steps: Define TicketInput and TriageDecision BaseModel schemas using Literal/Enum categories and bounded confidence scores.
Add @field_validator and @model_validator rules (e.g., refund_amount requires order_id).
Write tests feeding valid, partial, and adversarial LLM JSON outputs through model_validate_json().
acceptanceCriteria: Invalid categories, missing required IDs, or out-of-range scores raise ValidationError cleanly.
Validation errors route to a safe fallback review queue rather than crashing the API.
JSON Schema exported via model_json_schema() matches expected LLM output format.

masteryChecklist: I know why Python type hints alone do not validate data at runtime.
I use Pydantic BaseModel, Field constraints, Literal/Enum, and nested models.
I write custom field and model validators and handle ValidationError gracefully.
I remember that valid JSON syntax does NOT prove an LLM output is factually true.

modules.title: LangChain Foundations
modules.subtitle: Understand LangChain abstractions, model interfaces, structured output, tools, inspection, and when plain Python wins.
modules.outcome: Use LangChain selectively for model portability, structured output, and tool schemas while inspecting intermediate calls and avoiding abstraction bloat.
modules.prerequisiteRationale: Only makes sense after learning direct LLM calls (M06) and Pydantic schemas (M07) so abstractions remain transparent.

miniProject.title: Portable Triage Chain vs. Plain Python Comparison
miniProject.brief: Implement the support triage classifier using LangChain model + with_structured_output(TriageDecision) and compare readability, testability, and trace visibility against plain Python.
steps: Create a model-agnostic chat model wrapper with structured Pydantic output.
Define a read-only customer-lookup tool schema and inspect generated tool calls.
Write a short engineering decision note on when LangChain saves effort vs adds indirection.
acceptanceCriteria: Intermediate prompt, tool call, and raw token usage are logged clearly.
Pydantic contract validation enforces output shape.
Side-by-side comparison documents trade-offs against direct SDK/HTTP calls.

masteryChecklist: I know what LangChain provides (model interfaces, messages, tools, retrievers) and what it hides.
I can attach Pydantic structured outputs and inspect intermediate tool calls.
I understand how LangChain's create_agent runs on LangGraph under the hood.
I choose plain Python when a single direct API call is simpler and clearer.

modules.title: Retrieval and RAG
modules.subtitle: Design document loading, chunking, embeddings, hybrid search, metadata ACL filtering, attribution, and retrieval evals.
modules.outcome: Build grounded retrieval pipelines that enforce access control, cite sources, handle deletions, and evaluate retrieval separately from generation.
modules.prerequisiteRationale: Needs LLM context limits (M06), Pydantic metadata schemas (M07), and retriever abstractions (M08).

miniProject.title: Help-Center Grounded Retrieval Pipeline
miniProject.brief: Index a set of support policy Markdown docs with metadata (product, audience, updated_at), implement hybrid keyword+semantic search with ACL filtering, and test citation accuracy.
steps: Chunk help articles cleanly by section heading while preserving source URL and tenant metadata.
Implement metadata filtering so internal-only runbooks never leak into customer replies.
Measure Recall@K on 10 representative support queries before touching the answer prompt.
acceptanceCriteria: Retrieved chunks carry verifiable doc IDs and section titles.
Unauthorized tenant or internal documents are excluded before context assembly.
Retrieval metrics are measured independently of LLM prose quality.

masteryChecklist: I know when retrieval (RAG) is better than prompt stuffing or fine-tuning.
I design chunk boundaries and metadata filters for precision and access control.
I combine keyword and vector search (hybrid retrieval) and understand reranking.
I know why RAG reduces but never completely eliminates hallucinations.

modules.title: LangGraph Fundamentals
modules.subtitle: Build explicit stateful graphs with nodes, conditional edges, reducers, checkpointing, interrupts, and safe side effects.
modules.outcome: Architect durable, resumable workflows using LangGraph State, Nodes, Conditional Edges, Checkpointers, and Human-in-the-Loop interrupts.
modules.prerequisiteRationale: LangGraph builds directly on typed state schemas (M07), model/tool interfaces (M08), and retrieval steps (M09).

miniProject.title: Human-Approved Triage State Graph
miniProject.brief: Build a LangGraph StateGraph that classifies a support email, retrieves policy chunks, pauses at an interrupt() before sending an external reply, and resumes cleanly after human approval.
steps: Define a typed graph State with message reducer and explicit approval fields.
Add deterministic validation, retrieval, draft, and conditional routing edges.
Attach a checkpointer, trigger interrupt() before email dispatch, and resume with Command(resume=...).
acceptanceCriteria: Graph enforces a hard maximum step/retry limit and clean termination edge.
State survives pause/resume across separate invocations using a thread_id.
Side-effect node executes only after explicit approval and remains idempotent.

masteryChecklist: I model shared workflow state with explicit channels and reducers.
I combine deterministic Python nodes and conditional routing with LLM steps.
I implement persistence checkpoints and human-approval interrupts safely.
I know when to use a StateGraph vs a simple chain vs an autonomous agent.

modules.title: Agent Engineering
modules.subtitle: Enforce strict tool permissions, loop/budget caps, prompt-injection defenses, escalation paths, and single-vs-multi-agent discipline.
modules.outcome: Engineer bounded agents that resist untrusted prompt injection, validate tool arguments, escalate ambiguity, and earn autonomy only where justified.
modules.prerequisiteRationale: Requires retrieval trust boundaries (M09) and explicit graph state/interrupt control (M10).

miniProject.title: Hardened Support Agent Guardrail Harness
miniProject.brief: Take an unbounded tool-calling agent and harden it with least-privilege tool schemas, max iteration/token budgets, prompt-injection isolation, and human escalation rules.
steps: Separate read-only tools from write/destructive tools requiring human confirmation.
Test the agent against malicious instructions hidden inside retrieved support attachments.
Enforce iteration budget, tool-result Pydantic checks, and automatic escalation on missing info.
acceptanceCriteria: Injected instructions in retrieved documents cannot trigger unauthorized tool calls.
Agent terminates gracefully when step or token budget is reached.
Missing account data triggers clarification/escalation instead of guessing.

masteryChecklist: I scope agent tool permissions using least privilege and confirm risky writes.
I defend against prompt injection in user inputs and retrieved documents.
I enforce loop limits, cost caps, and deterministic validation of tool arguments.
I understand why adding more agents often reduces reliability compared to a well-structured single workflow.

modules.title: n8n + Python + AI Integration
modules.subtitle: Split orchestration cleanly between n8n and FastAPI using service auth, async jobs, callbacks, idempotency, and dead-letter queues.
modules.outcome: Architect production hybrid systems where n8n handles triggers/SaaS glue and FastAPI owns Pydantic contracts, AI logic, retries, and approval callbacks.
modules.prerequisiteRationale: Unifies FastAPI + n8n HTTP bridges (M05), Pydantic contracts (M07), and LangGraph approvals (M10).

miniProject.title: Async n8n-to-FastAPI Support Pipeline
miniProject.brief: Connect an n8n Email/Webhook trigger to a FastAPI async job endpoint that immediately returns 202 Accepted, processes via LangGraph, calls back an n8n Webhook for Slack/email approval, and logs dead-letter failures.
steps: Keep trigger, CRM connectors, and Slack notifications in n8n; move validation, RAG, and AI triage to FastAPI.
Authenticate n8n -> FastAPI requests with scoped API key / HMAC signature and FastAPI -> n8n callbacks.
Implement idempotency keys and a failure queue workflow in n8n for unrecoverable errors.
acceptanceCriteria: Long-running AI jobs never time out n8n HTTP Request nodes (uses 202 + callback pattern).
Duplicate webhook deliveries from email/SaaS providers produce only one ticket action.
Failed payloads land in an inspectable failure queue rather than disappearing silently.

masteryChecklist: I know what belongs in n8n vs what belongs in a Python FastAPI service.
I implement shared-secret or signed webhook authentication between n8n and Python.
I design async 202 + callback patterns to avoid HTTP request timeouts.
I separate retry boundaries and route poisoned payloads to failure queues.

modules.title: Evaluation and Observability
modules.subtitle: Build test datasets, measure extraction/retrieval/tool metrics, prevent regressions, trace latency/cost, and redact PII.
modules.outcome: Prove whether prompt, retrieval, or model changes actually improved quality using deterministic evaluations, traces, and privacy-safe logs.
modules.prerequisiteRationale: Evaluates the LLM calls (M06), RAG retrieval (M09), and agent tool choices (M11) built in earlier modules.

miniProject.title: Automated Triage Eval & Trace Suite
miniProject.brief: Create a 25-case labeled JSON dataset (normal, edge, and adversarial tickets), run automated pytest evaluations for classification accuracy, retrieval recall, and tool-arg correctness, and log redacted traces.
steps: Curate realistic ticket test cases including multi-intent, angry tone, missing IDs, and prompt-injection payloads.
Separate retrieval metrics (Recall@K) from classification precision/recall and tool-call schema checks.
Verify PII scrubbing removes email addresses/tokens from logs while keeping correlation IDs.
acceptanceCriteria: Eval suite runs deterministically in CI/local pytest and prints per-category score breakdown.
Logs capture latency, token cost, and model version without raw PII secrets.
Prompt/model comparison table prevents shipping regressions based on gut feel.

masteryChecklist: I curate representative golden and adversarial datasets instead of cherry-picking examples.
I evaluate retrieval quality separately from final LLM generation quality.
I monitor latency, cost per run, and error rates using privacy-aware structured traces.
I treat LLM self-reported confidence scores skeptically unless calibrated empirically.

modules.title: Deployment, Cloudflare, and Security
modules.subtitle: Package with Docker, configure secrets safely, understand DNS/reverse proxies/TLS, Cloudflare Tunnel vs Access vs Workers, and backups.
modules.outcome: Ship containerized AI automation services securely behind reverse proxies or Cloudflare Tunnel + Access with least privilege and verified backups.
modules.prerequisiteRationale: Applies networking/TLS/Docker basics (M03) and hybrid n8n+FastAPI services (M05, M12) to production hosting.

miniProject.title: Containerized Production Deployment Blueprint
miniProject.brief: Write a production Dockerfile, Compose config with healthchecks, non-root user, env secret injection, reverse proxy / n8n N8N_WEBHOOK_URL config, and Cloudflare Tunnel + Access security architecture.
steps: Containerize the FastAPI service with a non-root user, explicit /health check, and pinned dependencies.
Configure reverse proxy / Cloudflare Tunnel routing without exposing raw database or internal ports publicly.
Add Cloudflare Access / bearer token auth verification and document backup/restore steps.
acceptanceCriteria: No secrets are baked into Dockerfile or Docker image layers.
Application verifies its own bearer/service auth even behind Cloudflare Tunnel.
Health checks, TLS termination, and backup restoration procedure are documented and testable.

masteryChecklist: I distinguish DNS, CDN caching, origin hosting, Cloudflare Tunnel, Cloudflare Access, and Workers.
I never treat Cloudflare Tunnel alone as application authentication.
I package services in Docker with health checks, non-root users, and externalized secrets.
I configure n8n reverse-proxy variables (N8N_WEBHOOK_URL, N8N_PROXY_HOPS) and plan backups.

modules.title: Production Engineering and Career Portfolio
modules.subtitle: Scope narrow business problems, define SLOs and cost budgets, plan rollbacks, measure real outcomes, and present honest case studies.
modules.outcome: Operate AI automations sustainably with clear ownership, rollback runbooks, cost ceilings, verified ROI measurement, and interview-ready portfolio case studies.
modules.prerequisiteRationale: Synthesizes evaluation/observability (M13) and production deployment/security (M14) into end-to-end engineering ownership.

miniProject.title: Production Runbook & Honest Portfolio Case Study
miniProject.brief: Package one of your capstone projects with a 1-page architecture doc, SLOs, monthly token/hosting budget, rollback drill, data-retention policy, and an honest portfolio case study.
steps: Write an architecture decision record explaining why each tool (n8n, FastAPI, Pydantic, RAG, LangGraph) was chosen or skipped.
Define latency/availability SLOs, cost alerts, rollback steps, and data-retention timelines.
Draft an interview walkthrough highlighting trade-offs, measured evaluation results, and failure lessons.
acceptanceCriteria: Case study states only real measured test/eval results and avoids fabricated percentages.
Rollback plan lets operators revert prompts, models, or routing within minutes.
Maintenance owner, alert channel, and cost ceiling are explicitly assigned.

masteryChecklist: I scope high-value, narrow automation problems instead of vague 'AI everything' pitches.
I define service objectives, cost budgets, data retention, and rollback procedures.
I measure real baseline vs post-automation outcomes honestly.
I can defend my architectural trade-offs and failure modes in engineering interviews.
